questions.question: Area of the floor of a cubical room is 48 m². The length of the longest rod that can be kept in that room is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Longest rod in a cubical room = √(3 × Area of floor)

Given: Area of floor = 48 m²

Length of rod = √(3 × 48) = √144

Length of rod = 12 m

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the floor (a²) = 48 m²

**Formula Used:**

Side of cube (a) = √(Floor Area)

Length of longest rod (Space Diagonal) = a√3

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ec524d0de71a8a1d41dd6f41deb653f0da8a1f4a130fd5f534f211a2417b4631.png] 

⇒ Area of square floor = a² = 48

⇒ Side of the cubical room (a) = √48 m

⇒ Length of longest rod = √(a² + a² + a²) = √(3a²)

⇒ Length = √(3 × 48)

⇒ Length = √144

⇒ Length = 12 m

**∴ The correct answer is 12 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Cube

The total space occupied by the cube is given by side³ (a×a×a).

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The sum of areas of all 6 square faces is 6a².

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The area of the four vertical walls (excluding floor and ceiling) is 4a².

Diagonal of a Cuboid

For a room with length (l), width (w), and height (h), the longest rod is √(l² + w² + h²).</p

questions.question: A person walked from a village to a hospital at a speed of 30 km/h and walked back at a speed of 2 km/h. If the whole journey took 4 h 36 min, find the distance of the hospital from the village.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total time = 4 h 36 min = 4.6 hours

Shortcut formula: Distance = [ (Product of Speeds) ÷ (Sum of Speeds) ] × Total Time

Distance = [ (30 × 2) ÷ (30 + 2) ] × 4.6

Distance = [ 60 ÷ 32 ] × 4.6 = 1.875 × 4.6 = 8.625 km

8.625 km = 8 5/8 km

**∴ The correct answer is 8 5/8 km.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Village to Hospital (s₁) = 30 km/h

Speed from Hospital to Village (s₂) = 2 km/h

Total time taken = 4 h 36 min

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f7c88935600c168e204ab077cdc8e2f1b628d0b01d1c38c600bcd6f19d279395.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Time = 4 h + (36 ÷ 60) h = 4 + 3/5 = 23/5 hours

⇒ Let the distance be d km.

⇒ (d ÷ 30) + (d ÷ 2) = 23/5

⇒ (d + 15d) ÷ 30 = 23/5

⇒ 16d ÷ 30 = 23/5

⇒ 16d = (23 × 30) ÷ 5

⇒ 16d = 23 × 6

⇒ 16d = 138

⇒ d = 138 ÷ 16 = 69 ÷ 8

⇒ d = 8 5/8 km

**∴ The correct answer is 8 5/8 km.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Constant Distance

When an object covers the same distance at two different speeds s₁ and s₂, the average speed = (2 × s₁ × s₂) ÷ (s₁ + s₂).

Speed-Time Relationship

If distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (s₁ ÷ s₂ = t₂ ÷ t₁). Ratio of speeds 30:2 = 15:1 implies ratio of times is 1:15.

Unit Conversion

To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18.</p

questions.question: What is the value of 0.4 × 0.5 + 2 × (0.10 - 0.5)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Expression = 0.4 times 0.5 + 2 times (0.10 - 0.5)

**Formula used:**

BODMAS Rule (Brackets, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction)

**Calculations:**

0.4 times 0.5 + 2 times (0.10 - 0.5)

⇒ 0.4 times 0.5 + 2 times (-0.4)

⇒ 0.2 + (-0.8)

⇒ 0.2 - 0.8

⇒ -0.60

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: PQRS is a cyclic quadrilateral in which ∠P = (2x + 7°) ,∠Q = (x + 12°),∠R = (4y – 7°), and ∠S = (5y + 3°). Find the value of (x + y)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles sum to 180°.

∠P + ∠R = 180° → (2x + 7) + (4y − 7) = 180 → x + 2y = 90

∠Q + ∠S = 180° → (x + 12) + (5y + 3) = 180 → x + 5y = 165

Subtracting the equations: (x + 5y) − (x + 2y) = 165 − 90 → 3y = 75 → y = 25

Substituting y: x + 2(25) = 90 → x = 40

x + y = 40 + 25 = 65°

**∴ The correct answer is 65°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: ∠P = (2x + 7°), ∠Q = (x + 12°), ∠R = (4y − 7°), and ∠S = (5y + 3°).

Formula Used: In a cyclic quadrilateral, ∠P + ∠R = 180° and ∠Q + ∠S = 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/56b4db1e069f2f4c65820ecd73c2c97f59101a0203735905f36dbdbe0cab61f2.png] 

⇒ ∠P + ∠R = 180°

⇒ (2x + 7°) + (4y − 7°) = 180°

⇒ 2x + 4y = 180°

⇒ x + 2y = 90° ---- (Eq. 1)

⇒ ∠Q + ∠S = 180°

⇒ (x + 12°) + (5y + 3°) = 180°

⇒ x + 5y + 15° = 180°

⇒ x + 5y = 165° ---- (Eq. 2)

⇒ Subtracting (Eq. 1) from (Eq. 2):

⇒ (x + 5y) − (x + 2y) = 165° − 90°

⇒ 3y = 75°

⇒ y = 25°

⇒ Substitute y = 25° in (Eq. 1):

⇒ x + 2(25°) = 90°

⇒ x + 50° = 90°

⇒ x = 40°

⇒ Value of (x + y) = 40° + 25° = 65°

**∴ The correct answer is 65°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

A quadrilateral is cyclic if and only if its opposite angles are supplementary, i.e., sum is 180°.

Exterior Angle of Cyclic Quadrilateral

The exterior angle formed by extending one side of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior opposite angle.

Ptolemy Theorem

For a cyclic quadrilateral with sides a, b, c, d and diagonals p, q: (p × q) = (a × c) + (b × d).</p

questions.question: Satish bought 35 notebooks for Rs. 700 and sold 28 of them for Rs. 600. Find his percentage gain.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

CP of 1 notebook = 700 ÷ 35 = ₹20

SP of 1 notebook = 600 ÷ 28 = ₹150/7

Ratio CP : SP = 20 : 150/7 = 140 : 150 = 14 : 15

Gain % = [(15 − 14) ÷ 14] × 100 = 100/14 = 50/7%

50/7% = 7 1/7%

**∴ The correct answer is 7 1/7%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total notebooks bought = 35

Cost Price (CP) for 35 notebooks = ₹700

Selling Price (SP) for 28 notebooks = ₹600

**Formula Used:**

Gain % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/830af17c2054e60ca84987afc55e9235e37207eed82932624acbd268a74461cd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CP of 1 notebook = 700 ÷ 35 = ₹20

⇒ SP of 1 notebook = 600 ÷ 28 = ₹150/7

⇒ Profit = SP − CP = 150/7 − 20

⇒ Profit = (150 − 140) ÷ 7 = ₹10/7

⇒ Gain % = [(10/7) ÷ 20] × 100

⇒ Gain % = (10 ÷ 140) × 100

⇒ Gain % = 100/14 = 50/7%

⇒ Gain % = 7 1/7%

**∴ The correct answer is 7 1/7%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Fundamentals

Profit occurs when SP > CP. Gain = SP − CP. Loss occurs when CP > SP. Loss = CP − SP.

Percentage Calculations

Gain% = (Gain/CP) × 100. Loss% = (Loss/CP) × 100. Both are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

questions.question: The mean of 15 numbers is 30. If 3 is added to each number, then what will be the new mean?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If a constant 'k' is added to each observation in a data set, the mean of the data set also increases by the same constant 'k'.

New Mean = Old Mean + k

New Mean = 30 + 3 = 33

**∴ The correct answer is 33.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers (n) = 15

Mean of 15 numbers = 30

Value added to each number = 3

**Formula Used:**

Mean = Sum of observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e13f4e5e966a2064176d354b2d27061bbc9d33ffaed0b695a22a8b3df3cb993.png] 

⇒ Sum of original 15 numbers = Mean × n = 30 × 15 = 450

⇒ If 3 is added to each of the 15 numbers, total increase = 15 × 3 = 45

⇒ New Sum = 450 + 45 = 495

⇒ New Mean = New Sum ÷ 15

⇒ New Mean = 495 ÷ 15 = 33

**∴ The correct answer is 33.**

**__Additional Information__**

Effect of Operations on Mean

If every observation is multiplied by k, the new mean becomes k × Old Mean. If every observation is divided by k (k ≠ 0), the new mean becomes Old Mean ÷ k.

Linear Transformation of Mean

If Y = aX + b, then Mean(Y) = a × Mean(X) + b. This shows that mean is sensitive to both change of scale (multiplication) and change of origin (addition).

Sum of Deviations

The sum of deviations of a set of observations from their arithmetic mean is always zero. Σ(xᵢ − Mean) = 0.</p

questions.question:
A dice is thrown 150 times, with the frequencies for the outcomes 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 being as given in the following table. How many times is the number appearing on the dice a prime number?

 
 

 Outcome
 1
 2
 3
 4
 5
 6
 
 

 Frequency
 23
 43
 33
 13
 10
 28
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Identify prime numbers on a dice: 2, 3, and 5.

Sum their corresponding frequencies from the table.

Total frequency of prime numbers = 43 + 33 + 10 = 86.

**∴ The correct answer is 86.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given Data from Frequency Table:

Frequency of Outcome 1 = 23

Frequency of Outcome 2 = 43

Frequency of Outcome 3 = 33

Frequency of Outcome 4 = 13

Frequency of Outcome 5 = 10

Frequency of Outcome 6 = 28

Total Throws = 150

Prime numbers in the set {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}:

⇒ 1 is neither prime nor composite.

⇒ 2 is a prime number.

⇒ 3 is a prime number.

⇒ 4 is a composite number (2 × 2).

⇒ 5 is a prime number.

⇒ 6 is a composite number (2 × 3).

Calculation for prime number frequency:

⇒ Total prime frequency = Freq(2) + Freq(3) + Freq(5)

⇒ Total prime frequency = 43 + 33 + 10

⇒ Total prime frequency = 86

**∴ The correct answer is 86.**

**__Additional Information__**

Definition of Prime Numbers

A prime number is a natural number greater than 1 that has no positive divisors other than 1 and itself. The first few are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11...

Special Case of 1

The number 1 is not considered a prime number because it does not have exactly two distinct divisors; it only has one divisor (1).

Probability of Prime Numbers

The experimental probability P(Prime) = (Total frequency of prime outcomes) ÷ (Total number of trials). In this case, P(Prime) = 86 ÷ 150 = 43/75.</p

questions.question: If xy(x + y) = 1, then the value of 1/(x3y³) - x³ - y³ is
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given xy(x + y) = 1 ⇒ x + y = 1/xy

Replace 1/(x³y³) with (x + y)³ in the expression.

Expression becomes: (x + y)³ − x³ − y³ = 3xy(x + y)

Substitute xy(x + y) = 1: 3 × 1 = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: xy(x + y) = 1

Formula Used: (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

⇒ xy(x + y) = 1

⇒ x + y = 1 / (xy)

⇒ (x + y)³ = (1 / xy)³ [Cubing both sides]

⇒ x³ + y³ + 3xy(x + y) = 1 / (x³y³)

⇒ 3xy(x + y) = 1 / (x³y³) − x³ − y³

⇒ 3(1) = 1 / (x³y³) − x³ − y³ [Since xy(x + y) = 1]

⇒ 1 / (x³y³) − x³ − y³ = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Cubic Identity

The expansion of (x + y)³ is x³ + y³ + 3xy(x + y), which relates the sum of cubes to the product and sum of variables.

Sum of Three Cubes

If x + y + z = 0, then x³ + y³ + z³ = 3xyz. This is a special case of the identity a³+b³+c³−3abc = (a+b+c)(a²+b²+c²−ab−bc−ca).

Reciprocal Identity

If x + 1/x = k, then x³ + 1/x³ = k³ − 3k. This shortcut is frequently used in banking and SSC exams for quantitative aptitude.</p

questions.question: Two corresponding angles formed by the intersection of two parallel lines by a transversal are x and 70°. Then, the value of 4x - 30° is ;
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Corresponding angles of parallel lines are always equal.

∴ x = 70°

Substitute x in the required expression: 4x − 30°

4(70°) − 30° = 280° − 30° = 250°

**∴ The correct answer is 250°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Parallel lines are intersected by a transversal.

Corresponding angles are x and 70°.

**Formula Used:**

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the pairs of corresponding angles are equal in measure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/be2e8f354f36a9f0eb7887fb204af1bffbe5b0e8a18a227fea1c217120ac449c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ x = 70° (Property of corresponding angles)

⇒ To find: 4x − 30°

⇒ 4 × 70° − 30°

⇒ 280° − 30°

⇒ 250°

**∴ The correct answer is 250°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Alternate Interior Angles

Angles on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines are equal.

Consecutive Interior Angles

Angles on the same side of the transversal and between parallel lines are supplementary (Sum = 180°).

Vertically Opposite Angles

When two lines intersect, the angles opposite each other at the vertex are always equal.

Linear Pair

Angles that are adjacent and form a straight line add up to 180°.</p

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is divisible by 9?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

Testing the options by calculating the digit sum:

3915 → 3 + 9 + 1 + 5 = 18.

Since 18 is divisible by 9, the number 3915 is also divisible by 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 3915.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Numbers (1) 3739, (2) 3661, (3) 3659, (4) 3915.

Formula Used: Divisibility rule of 9 ⇒ Sum of digits must be a multiple of 9.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a0674499e16f8e448ec311c398c0620e825e39a3f167b1d4f9be5edd24f7020d.png] 

⇒ Option 1: 3 + 7 + 3 + 9 = 22 (Not divisible by 9)

⇒ Option 2: 3 + 6 + 6 + 1 = 16 (Not divisible by 9)

⇒ Option 3: 3 + 6 + 5 + 9 = 23 (Not divisible by 9)

⇒ Option 4: 3 + 9 + 1 + 5 = 18 (18 ÷ 9 = 2, exactly divisible)

**∴ The correct answer is 3915.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. For example, 123 (1+2+3=6) is divisible by 3.

Divisibility by 11

The difference between the sum of digits at odd places and even places must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a number that is divisible by 4. For example, 512 is divisible by 4 as 12 is divisible by 4.</p

questions.question:
In the given figure if ∠P = 70° and ∠PSR = 100°, then ∠T =

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f8b703a2604296f435e9d85187bbdd7ead4955a2a0aa73b7eef2740f4d5123bd.png]
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS, opposite angles are supplementary.

∠PQR + ∠PSR = 180° ⇒ ∠PQR = 180° − 100° = 80°.

In ΔPQT, sum of angles is 180°.

∠T = 180° − (∠P + ∠PQR) = 180° − (70° + 80°) = 30°.

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** ∠P = 70° and ∠PSR = 100° in the cyclic quadrilateral PQRS within ΔPQT.

**Formula Used:** Sum of opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral is 180°; Sum of angles in a triangle is 180°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d554961db59dc38ee8329bbc499f8316df30e5e9a6dd463f140f9dba3613947.png] 

In cyclic quadrilateral PQRS:

⇒ ∠PQR + ∠PSR = 180°

⇒ ∠PQR + 100° = 180°

⇒ ∠PQR = 180° − 100° = 80°

Now, consider the triangle ΔPQT:

⇒ ∠P + ∠PQT + ∠T = 180°

⇒ 70° + 80° + ∠T = 180°

⇒ 150° + ∠T = 180°

⇒ ∠T = 180° − 150°

⇒ ∠T = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Quadrilateral Property

A quadrilateral is cyclic if all its vertices lie on a single circle. The sum of opposite angles is always 180° (∠A + ∠C = 180° and ∠B + ∠D = 180°).

Exterior Angle of Cyclic Quadrilateral

The exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral is equal to the interior opposite angle. For example, if side PS is extended to T, then ∠TSR = ∠PQR.

Angle Sum Property of Triangle

For any triangle, the sum of all three interior angles is always exactly 180°.</p

questions.question: A, B and C are employed to do a piece of work for Rs. 420. A and B together are supposed to do 17/21 of the work and B&C together 6/21 of the work. What amount should A be paid?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work units = 21 (Denominator of fractions)

Work done by A + B = 17 units and Work done by B + C = 6 units

Total work (A + B + C) = 21 units

Work done by B = (A + B) + (B + C) − (A + B + C) = 17 + 6 − 21 = 2 units

Work done by A = (A + B) − B = 17 − 2 = 15 units

A's share = (Work by A ÷ Total Work) × Total Wage = (15 ÷ 21) × 420 = ₹300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount to be paid = ₹420

Work done by A and B together = 17/21

Work done by B and C together = 6/21

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4a2907bb663576292735702153b88a38cc95b5ed288cd47497bc8b6d01d8cfa6.png] 

**Formula:** Wage of a person = (Work done by the person / Total work) × Total amount

⇒ Total work = 1

⇒ Work done by (A + B + C) = 1

⇒ Work done by C = Total work − Work done by (A + B)

⇒ Work done by C = 1 − 17/21 = 4/21

⇒ Work done by B = Work done by (B + C) − Work done by C

⇒ Work done by B = 6/21 − 4/21 = 2/21

⇒ Work done by A = Work done by (A + B) − Work done by B

⇒ Work done by A = 17/21 − 2/21 = 15/21

⇒ Amount paid to A = (15/21) × 420

⇒ Amount paid to A = 15 × 20

⇒ Amount paid to A = ₹300

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Wage Distribution Rule

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each individual. If time is constant, wages are proportional to efficiency.

Individual Work Calculation

To find an individual's work from overlapping groups: Individual B = (Group A+B) + (Group B+C) − Total (A+B+C).

Efficiency and Time

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a work. Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time.

questions.question: Given a linear equation in two variables: 5x + 7y - 8 = 0, which of the following linear equations, along with the given equation, forms a system of linear equations having no solution?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a system of linear equations to have no solution, the lines must be parallel.

Condition: a₁/a₂ = b₁/b₂ ≠ c₁/c₂

Compare the given equation 5x + 7y − 8 = 0 with Option 1: 5x + 7y − 16 = 0.

We get 5/5 = 7/7 ≠ −8/−16 ⇒ 1 = 1 ≠ 1/2. This perfectly satisfies the no solution condition.

**∴ The correct answer is 5x + 7y - 16 = 0.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Equation 1: 5x + 7y − 8 = 0

Here, a₁ = 5, b₁ = 7, c₁ = −8

**Formula Used:**

For equations a₁x + b₁y + c₁ = 0 and a₂x + b₂y + c₂ = 0 to have no solution (parallel lines):

Condition: a₁/a

questions.question: The amount obtained by investing a certain sum at r% p.a. for 3 years at simple interest is equal to the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate for 13 years. The value of r is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Amount (3 years) = Simple Interest (13 years)

Principal + SI (3 years) = SI (13 years)

Principal = SI (13 years) − SI (3 years) = SI (10 years)

For Principal (100%) to be equal to 10 years of interest, the annual rate must be 100% ÷ 10 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given: Principal = P, Rate = r% p.a., Time₁ = 3 years, Time₂ = 13 years.

Formula: Simple Interest (SI) = (P × r × t) / 100 | Amount (A) = P + SI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e552677647a3c1a5a8ccc89628e0ec8f32a92be16f78caf004cf79d8fcf6f1a6.png] 

⇒ Amount after 3 years = P + (P × r × 3) / 100

⇒ Simple Interest for 13 years = (P × r × 13) / 100

⇒ According to the question: P + 3Pr/100 = 13Pr/100

⇒ P = 13Pr/100 − 3Pr/100

⇒ P = 10Pr/100

⇒ 1 = 10r/100

⇒ 1 = r/10

⇒ r = 10

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Basics

Simple Interest is calculated only on the principal amount. The formula is SI = P × R × T / 100, where P is Principal, R is Rate, and T is Time.

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount (A) at the end of the period is the sum of the principal and interest: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT/100).

Effective Rate of Interest

The effective interest earned over T years is (R × T)% of the principal. In this problem, the difference in time (13 − 3 = 10 years) represents the principal itself.</p

questions.question: Two bells chime together at 12 noon. Then one bell chimes every 48 seconds, while the other chimes every 84 seconds. When, among the given options, will both the bells chime together?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 48 and 84 seconds = 12 × 4 × 7 = 336 seconds.

The bells chime together every 336 seconds.

From the options, check the duration from 12 noon: 7 p.m. = 7 hours = 7 × 3600 = 25,200 seconds.

25,200 ÷ 336 = 75 (Exactly divisible).

**∴ The correct answer is 7 p.m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Interval of Bell 1 = 48 seconds

Interval of Bell 2 = 84 seconds

Start Time = 12:00 noon

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d164ed289e645c3f5572b4c7639ce031c4aa8269507fe40c10f90f9e947b887.png] 

Formula used: LCM (Least Common Multiple) determines the simultaneous interval.

⇒ Prime factorization of 48 = 2⁴ × 3

⇒ Prime factorization of 84 = 2² × 3 × 7

⇒ LCM(48, 84) = 2⁴ × 3 × 7 = 16 × 21 = 336 seconds

⇒ To find when they chime together at one of the given hours, the total time must be a multiple of 336.

⇒ Checking 7 p.m.: Total time = 7 hours × 60 min × 60 sec = 25,200 seconds

⇒ Number of intervals = 25,200 ÷ 336 = 75 cycles

**∴ The correct answer is 7 p.m.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM in Periodic Events

LCM is used to find the next time multiple events occurring at different fixed intervals will happen simultaneously (e.g., traffic lights, bells, racers on a track).

Time Conversion

1 Hour = 3600 seconds | 1 Minute = 60 seconds. Always ensure units are consistent before calculating LCM.

Divisibility Rule

If a time duration T is a multiple of the LCM of two intervals, both events will coincide at the end of time T.</p

questions.question: 10 years ago, a man's age was 5 times of his son's age. 2 years hence, twice his age will be equal to 4 times the age of his son. What is the present age (in years) of the son?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio (Man : Son) 10 years ago = 5 : 1 (Difference = 4 units)

Ratio (Man : Son) 2 years hence = 4 : 2 = 2 : 1 (Difference = 1 unit)

Make difference equal: Multiply (2 : 1) by 4 ⇒ New Ratio = 8 : 4

Gap in Son's ratio units = 4 − 1 = 3 units. Total time gap = 10 + 2 = 12 years.

3 units = 12 years ⇒ 1 unit = 4 years.

Son's age 10 years ago = 1 unit = 4 years ⇒ Present age = 4 + 10 = 14 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 14 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the present age of the man be M and the son be S.

10 years ago: (M − 10) = 5 × (S − 10)

2 years hence: 2 × (M + 2) = 4 × (S + 2)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43f90f63387b96769133d990bb29bf4f23b0137d5d491dae2d2e74cad6675d4f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ M − 10 = 5S − 50

⇒ M = 5S − 40 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ 2(M + 2) = 4(S + 2)

⇒ M + 2 = 2(S + 2)

⇒ M + 2 = 2S + 4

⇒ M = 2S + 2 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ 5S − 40 = 2S + 2

⇒ 3S = 42

⇒ S = 42 ÷ 3

⇒ S = 14 years

**∴ The correct answer is 14 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two people remains constant throughout their lives, regardless of how many years pass.

Sum of Ages Change

If the sum of ages of N people is X today, then after Y years, the new sum will be X + (N × Y).

Ratio Balancing Method

To solve age problems using ratios, always ensure the difference between the ratio parts of two individuals is made equal across different time periods.</p

questions.question: Express sin 74° + tan 74° in terms of trigonometric ratios of angles between 0° and 45°.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To express angles between 0° and 45°, subtract the given angle from 90° and apply the complementary trigonometric ratios.

The complement of 74° is 90° − 74° = 16°.

Convert the respective trigonometric functions: sin → cos and tan → cot.

Thus, sin 74° + tan 74° directly becomes cos 16° + cot 16°.

**∴ The correct answer is cos 16° + cot 16°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: sin 74° + tan 74°

**Formula Used:**

sin(90° − θ) = cos θ

tan(90° − θ) = cot θ

**Calculations:**

⇒ We can express 74° in terms of its complementary angle as (90° − 16°).

⇒ sin 74° = sin(90° − 16°)

⇒ Applying the complementary identity, sin(90° − 16°) = cos 16°

⇒ tan 74° = tan(90° − 16°)

⇒ Applying the complementary identity, tan(90° − 16°) = cot 16°

⇒ Substitute these new values back into the original expression.

⇒ sin 74° + tan 74° = cos 16° + cot 16°

**∴ The correct answer is cos 16° + cot 16°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Complementary Angles in Trigonometry

Two angles that sum up to exactly 90° are known as complementary. The interrelated trigonometric pairs are sine & cosine, tangent & cotangent, and secant & cosecant.

Trigonometric Signs by Quadrant

In the first quadrant, which encompasses all angles from 0° to 90°, every basic trigonometric function naturally yields a positive value.

Basic Pythagorean Identities

The foundational formulas connecting the squares of trigonometric functions are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.
</p

questions.question: A group of men decided to do a job in 11 days but 16 men left the work after each day. The work, as a result, got completed in 15 days. How many men were there initially in the group?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work planned = 11 × M (where M is initial men).

Actual work done = Sum of men over 15 days = $\frac{15}{2}$ [2M + (15 − 1)(−16)].

11M = 15M − 1680.

4M = 1680 ⇒ M = 420.

**∴ The correct answer is 420 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Planned completion time = 11 days

Actual completion time = 15 days

Number of men leaving daily = 16

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Number of Men × Number of Days

Sum of Arithmetic Progression (Sₙ) = $\frac{n}{2}$ [2a + (n − 1)d]

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency (Avg Men)**
 
 

 Planned Group
 11
 11x
 x
 
 

 Actual Group
 15
 x − 112
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial number of men be x.

⇒ Total work planned = 11 × x = 11x man-days.

⇒ Actual work is the sum of men over 15 days: x + (x − 16) + (x − 32) + ... up to 15 terms.

⇒ Total work done = $\frac{15}{2}$ [2x + (15 − 1) × (−16)]

⇒ 11x = $\frac{15}{2}$ [2x − 224]

⇒ 11x = 15 × (x − 112)

⇒ 11x = 15x − 1680

⇒ 4x = 1680

⇒ x = 420

**∴ The correct answer is 420 men.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Man-Days Concept

Work is calculated as the product of the number of workers and the time taken (W = M × D). If the workforce is constant, M₁D₁ = M₂D₂.

Sum of Arithmetic Progression

When the number of workers changes by a constant amount each day, the total work is the sum of an AP: Sₙ = $\frac{n}{2}$[2a + (n − 1)d].

Average Workforce

In a linear decrease/increase of workers, the average number of workers per day is equal to the number of workers on the middle day of the period.</p

questions.question: If the diameter of the base of a cone is 42 cm and its curved surface area is 2310 cm², then what is 45% of the volume (in cm³)? (Take π = 22/7 )
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Radius r = 21 cm, CSA = 2310 cm².

Slant height l = CSA ÷ (π × r) = 2310 ÷ (22/7 × 21) = 35 cm.

Height h = √(35² − 21²) = 28 cm (using 3, 4, 5 triplet × 7).

45% of Vol = 0.45 × (1/3 × 22/7 × 21 × 21 × 28) = 0.45 × 12936 = 5821.2 cm³.

**∴ The correct answer is 5821.2 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter (d) = 42 cm ⇒ Radius (r) = 21 cm

Curved Surface Area (CSA) = 2310 cm²

π = 22/7

**Formula Used:**

CSA of Cone = π × r × l

Volume of Cone (V) = (1/3) × π × r² × h

Relation: l² = r² + h²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/609035e2e1436c8da4695b558c4f30c01e8ad1ba53bc4ac2d38a2897737ab3e3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ CSA = πrl ⇒ 2310 = (22/7) × 21 × l

⇒ 2310 = 66 × l

⇒ l = 2310 ÷ 66 = 35 cm

⇒ h = √(l² − r²) = √(35² − 21²)

⇒ h = √(1225 − 441) = √784 = 28 cm

⇒ Volume (V) = (1/3) × (22/7) × 21 × 21 × 28

⇒ V = 22 × 21 × 28 = 12936 cm³

⇒ Required Value = 45% of 12936 = (45/100) × 12936

⇒ Required Value = 0.45 × 12936 = 5821.2 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 5821.2 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cone

The total surface area includes the curved surface and the base area: TSA = πr(l + r).

Volume of Cylinder

The volume of a cone is exactly 1/3 the volume of a cylinder with the same radius and height: V = πr²h.

Pythagorean Triplets in Mensuration

For a cone, r, h, and l form a right-angled triangle. Common triplets like (3,4,5), (5,12,13), and (7,24,25) help find missing dimensions quickly.</p

questions.question: Find the greatest possible value of (a + b) for which the 8-digit number 143b203a is divisible by 15.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Divisibility by 15 requires divisibility by both 3 and 5.

For divisibility by 5, the last digit 'a' must be 0 or 5.

To maximize (a + b), we pick the largest 'a', so a = 5.

Sum of digits = 1 + 4 + 3 + b + 2 + 0 + 3 + 5 = 18 + b.

For divisibility by 3, (18 + b) must be a multiple of 3; the largest digit 'b' is 9.

Greatest (a + b) = 5 + 9 = 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given 8-digit number: 143b203a

Condition: Divisible by 15 (i.e., divisible by 3 and 5).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10567b8e03308cb734fc87e8e262dcbbabe65f905e33e5d6b409916b2d19c9df.png] 

⇒ Divisibility by 5: Last digit 'a' must be 0 or 5.

⇒ Divisibility by 3: Sum of digits = (1 + 4 + 3 + b + 2 + 0 + 3 + a) = (13 + a + b) must be divisible by 3.

⇒ Case 1: If a = 5 (largest possible last digit):

⇒ Sum = 13 + 5 + b = 18 + b.

⇒ For (18 + b) to be divisible by 3, possible values for b are 0, 3, 6, 9.

⇒ Maximum value of b = 9. So, (a + b) = 5 + 9 = 14.

⇒ Case 2: If a = 0:

⇒ Sum = 13 + 0 + b = 13 + b.

⇒ For (13 + b) to be divisible by 3, possible values for b are 2, 5, 8.

⇒ Maximum value of b = 8. So, (a + b) = 0 + 8 = 8.

⇒ Comparing Case 1 and Case 2, the greatest possible value of (a + b) is 14.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 3

A number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its individual digits is divisible by 3.

Divisibility by 5

A number is divisible by 5 if its unit digit (last digit) is either 0 or 5.

Divisibility by Composite Numbers

To check divisibility by a composite number n, check if it is divisible by its co-prime factors (e.g., 15 = 3 × 5, where HCF(3, 5) = 1).

Divisibility by 9

Similar to 3, a number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.</p

questions.question: Suppose A and B can complete a work together in 10 days. If B alone can complete the work in 15 days, then in how many days can A alone finish the work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Shortcut formula: Time for A alone = (Product of times) ÷ (Difference of times)

Time = (15 × 10) ÷ (15 − 10)

Time = 150 ÷ 5 = 30 days

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Time taken by (A + B) = 10 days, Time taken by B alone = 15 days.

Using LCM method to find Total Work and Efficiency:

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 A + B
 10
 30 (LCM of 10, 15)
 3
 
 

 B
 15
 2
 
 

⇒ Efficiency of (A + B) = 3 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = 2 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of A = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of B

⇒ Efficiency of A = 3 − 2 = 1 unit/day

⇒ Time taken by A alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of A

⇒ Time taken by A alone = 30 ÷ 1 = 30 days

**∴ The correct answer is 30 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If the ratio of efficiency of two workers is x:y, then the ratio of time taken by them to complete the same work will be y:x.

Total Work Formula

Total Work = Number of Days × Efficiency. This is a fundamental constant for a specific task when comparing different workers.

Fractional Work

If a person A can complete a work in 'n' days, then work done by A in 1 day = 1/n. If A and B work together, their 1-day work is 1/n₁ + 1/n₂.</p

questions.question: What will be the ratio of the amount received and the principal after 'n' years at the rate of 5% compound interest per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate of interest = 5% = 5/100 = 1/20.

For 1 year, the ratio of Principal (P) to Amount (A) is 20 : (20 + 1) = 20 : 21.

For 'n' years, the ratio P : A = 20ⁿ : 21ⁿ.

The question asks for the ratio of Amount to Principal (A : P).

A : P = 21ⁿ : 20ⁿ.

**∴ The correct answer is 21ⁿ : 20ⁿ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given:

Rate of interest (r) = 5% per annum

Time = n years

Formula used: A = P(1 + r/100)t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ee90f4bc468fab1aec983d9a71aac6b433309e22292ded27979345965f994b7a.png] 

Calculations:

⇒ A = P(1 + 5/100)ⁿ

⇒ A = P(1 + 1/20)ⁿ

⇒ A = P[(20 + 1)/20]ⁿ

⇒ A = P(21/20)ⁿ

⇒ A = P × (21ⁿ / 20ⁿ)

⇒ A / P = 21ⁿ / 20ⁿ

⇒ A : P = 21ⁿ : 20ⁿ

**∴ The correct answer is 21ⁿ : 20ⁿ.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The total interest earned is CI = A − P = P[(1 + r/100)ⁿ − 1].

Effective Rate of Interest

If interest is compounded semi-annually, the effective rate for a year is [ (1 + r/200)² − 1 ] × 100%.

Difference between SI and CI

For 2 years, the difference is D = P(r/100)². For 3 years, D = P(r/100)² × (3 + r/100).</p

questions.question: A seller sold a cloth for Rs.1008 after giving 20% discount on the labelled price. If he had not given the discount, then he would have earned a profit of 40% on the cost price. What is the cost price (in Rs.) of the cloth?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Selling Price is 80% of Marked Price (20% discount).

0.8 × MP = 1008 ⇒ MP = ₹1260

If no discount is given, MP becomes the new Selling Price, yielding a 40% profit.

1.4 × CP = 1260 ⇒ CP = 1260 ÷ 1.4 = ₹900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = ₹1008

⇒ Discount = 20%

⇒ Profit if sold without discount = 40%

**Formula Used:**

⇒ MP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 − Discount%)]

⇒ CP = SPₙₑw × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b6e92a77f95a7ffcda44ef20c292b35a50ee1358a347e8d285bb2e07cb1bfa0.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP = 1008 × [100 ÷ (100 − 20)]

⇒ MP = 1008 × (100 ÷ 80) = 1008 × (5 ÷ 4)

⇒ MP = 252 × 5 = ₹1260

⇒ If no discount is given, the article is sold at Marked Price.

⇒ New Selling Price (SPₙₑw) = MP = ₹1260

⇒ CP = 1260 × [100 ÷ (100 + 40)]

⇒ CP = 1260 × (100 ÷ 140) = 1260 × (5 ÷ 7)

⇒ CP = 180 × 5 = ₹900

**∴ The correct answer is ₹900.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP and MP

The direct ratio between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by the formula: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%).

Marked Price (MP)

It is the labelled or printed price of an article. Discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price, while Profit or Loss is strictly calculated on the Cost Price.

Zero Discount Scenario

When a seller gives no discount, the item is sold completely at its Marked Price. In this practical scenario, Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP).

questions.question: What is the smallest square number which is divisible by 4, 6 and 32?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 4, 6, and 32 = 96.

Prime factorization: 96 = 2⁵ × 3¹.

To make it a perfect square, exponents must be even.

Multiply 96 by (2¹ × 3¹) = 6.

Smallest square number = 96 × 6 = 576.

**∴ The correct answer is 576.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given numbers: 4, 6, 32

Method: Find the LCM and multiply it by factors required to complete prime factor pairs.

⇒ Prime factors of 4 = 2 × 2 = 2²

⇒ Prime factors of 6 = 2 × 3 = 2¹ × 3¹

⇒ Prime factors of 32 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 2⁵

⇒ LCM(4, 6, 32) = 2⁵ × 3¹ = 32 × 3 = 96

⇒ For a number to be a perfect square, all its prime factors must have even exponents.

⇒ Prime factors of 96 = 2⁵ × 3¹

⇒ To make exponents even, we need one more 2 and one more 3: (2⁵ × 2¹) × (3¹ × 3¹)

⇒ Required square number = 2⁶ × 3² = 64 × 9 = 576

**∴ The correct answer is 576.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest number that is a multiple of two or more numbers. It is found by taking the highest power of each prime factor present in the numbers.

Perfect Square Property

A number is a perfect square if the power of every prime factor in its prime factorization is an even integer (e.g., n = pa × qb where a and b are even).

Prime Factorization Method

Breaking down a composite number into a product of prime numbers to identify its fundamental building blocks.</p

questions.question: From the top of a tower, the angle of depression of the top of a 10 m high building is 60°. If the distance between the tower and the building is 50√3 m, find the height of the tower.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Angle of depression (θ) = 60° and horizontal distance (d) = 50√3 m.

Height difference between tower and building = d × tan(θ).

Height difference = 50√3 × √3 = 50 × 3 = 150 m.

Total tower height = Building height + Height difference = 10 + 150 = 160 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 160 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of building (h) = 10 m

Distance between tower and building (d) = 50√3 m

Angle of depression = 60°

**Formula Used:**

tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/91039c0be91a0eff684d79ee427e05f0b23057165790db6765574b4d91a8d928.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the height of the tower be H.

⇒ Let x be the height of the tower above the building level.

⇒ The angle of depression of the top of the building from the tower top is 60°.

⇒ This is equivalent to the angle of elevation of the tower top from the building top.

⇒ In the right-angled triangle formed above the building level:

⇒ tan 60° = x / 50√3

⇒ √3 = x / 50√3

⇒ x = 50√3 × √3

⇒ x = 50 × 3 = 150 m

⇒ Total height of tower (H) = x + height of building

⇒ H = 150 + 10 = 160 m

**∴ The correct answer is 160 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression and Elevation

The angle of depression from point A to point B is numerically equal to the angle of elevation from point B to point A because they are alternate interior angles.

Common Trigonometric Ratios

For height and distance problems: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, and tan 60° = √3.

Standard Height Formula

If two objects are separated by distance d, the height difference is given by h = d × tan(θ), where θ is the angle of elevation/depression between their tops.</p
